questions.stem: A pond contains water, dissolved minerals, sunlight, algae, water fleas, fish, and bacteria. A student needs to identify all the biotic factors. Which list contains ONLY biotic factors?

options.text: Water, sunlight, and dissolved minerals
Algae, water fleas, fish, and bacteria
Algae, water, fish, and sunlight
Water fleas, dissolved minerals, and bacteria

questions.explanation: Biotic factors are living components of an ecosystem. Algae, water fleas, fish, and bacteria are all living organisms. Water, sunlight, and dissolved minerals are abiotic (non-living) factors. A common mistake is forgetting that bacteria and algae are living organisms, or including water as biotic because organisms need it.

questions.stem: An ecologist studies a woodland and identifies: oak trees, squirrels, foxes, rabbits, bluebells, earthworms, and fungi. All the squirrels in the woodland represent a:

options.text: Community
Ecosystem
Population
Habitat

questions.explanation: A population is all the organisms of ONE species living in a particular area at a particular time. All the squirrels in the woodland form a population. A community includes ALL the different species in an area (squirrels, foxes, trees, etc. together). An ecosystem includes the community plus the abiotic factors. The habitat is the place where an organism lives.

questions.stem: After a drought reduces the water supply in a grassland ecosystem, the grass population declines. This then causes the rabbit population to decline, followed by a decline in the fox population. This is an example of:

options.text: An abiotic factor (water) affecting biotic factors through interdependence
Competition between foxes and rabbits for water
Predation causing the drought
A biotic factor affecting abiotic factors

questions.explanation: This demonstrates how abiotic factors (water availability) affect living organisms through a chain of interdependence. Reduced water limits grass growth (producer), which reduces rabbit food supply (primary consumer), which then reduces the food available for foxes (secondary consumer). Changes at one level cascade through the ecosystem because organisms depend on each other.

questions.stem: Two species of birds live in the same woodland. Species A nests in the treetops and eats insects from leaves. Species B nests in hedgerows and eats seeds from the ground. Why can these two species coexist in the same habitat?

options.text: They are the same species, so they do not compete
They occupy different ecological niches - they use different resources and different parts of the habitat, reducing competition
One species always outcompetes the other
Birds never compete with each other

questions.explanation: An ecological niche describes the role of an organism in its ecosystem, including what it eats, where it lives, and when it is active. These two bird species have different niches (different food sources, nesting locations), so they do not directly compete for the same resources. This allows them to coexist. If they had identical niches, one would outcompete the other (competitive exclusion).

questions.stem: A farmer drains a wetland to create farmland. Which statement best describes the ecological impact?

options.text: Only the water organisms are affected; land organisms will benefit
The ecosystem is destroyed because the abiotic conditions have changed, eliminating habitats for wetland species and reducing biodiversity
The organisms will simply move to another wetland nearby
Biodiversity will increase because farmland supports more species than wetlands

questions.explanation: Draining a wetland fundamentally changes the abiotic conditions (water availability, soil type, humidity). Species adapted to wetland conditions lose their habitat and cannot survive. Wetlands are among the most biodiverse ecosystems. While some organisms might relocate, many specialist species cannot. Farmland typically supports far fewer species than natural wetland, so biodiversity decreases significantly.
